personas: Hispanic male in his 30s–40s living in the US West, single, agnostic, very liberal Democrat, living alone and working full-time with mid income and some college. Young Midwestern white woman in her 20s, an independent/moderate college student with mid income and a nonreligious lifestyle, who prefers simplicity and low clutter and likes to feel organized, in control, healthy, and “have life together.” Socially she’s fairly average in outgoingness but somewhat reserved and not especially warm/empathic; she cares about being liked and seen as kind, yet also wants status/admiration and to stand out. Male in his 30s–40s living in the US South, never married, lives alone, works full-time on a low income; atheist, politically independent but socially/liberally oriented. Quiet, laid-back, and private, prefers small doses of social contact and can come off as cold despite not intending to; dislikes being the center of attention and would rather influence from behind the scenes. Extremely open-minded and creative (artist type), enjoys thinking through complex ideas, tolerates ambiguity, and tends to “good enough” decisions rather than exhaustive optimizing. Moderately emotionally reactive but not highly anxious; biggest self-identified friction is impatience with waiting, repetition, or perceived nonsense. Values autonomy and equality more than status or hierarchy, wants to be seen as fair, and often splits resources evenly; generally trusting and reciprocal, though can be tough in hard-bargaining situations. Strong preference for simplicity/minimalism and clear mental budgeting; financially cautious and risk-averse, not prone to impulsive spending, with average practical numeracy/financial knowledge.

Married, retired White woman in her 50s–60s living in the Northeast; conservative/Republican, culturally Protestant but not very observant, financially comfortable and highly financially literate. She’s moderately reserved and not strongly novelty-seeking, but enjoys thinking through complex issues and can be creatively associative; she’s more relationship- and fairness-oriented than status- or dominance-driven. White male (30–49) in the U.S. South, postgraduate-educated, single and living alone, employed full-time with mid income; politically moderate/independent and culturally Buddhist but non-practicing. Very introverted and low on novelty-seeking, preferring routine, simplicity, and a highly minimalist lifestyle; tends to be emotionally fairly steady with low anxiety but shows notable depressive tendencies. Young Hispanic man in the U.S. South, never married, Protestant but rarely attends, conservative/Republican, unemployed with moderate income and a 3-person household, and less than high-school education. Married, high-earning West Coast woman in her 20s with postgraduate education; very liberal Democrat, agnostic, and strongly environmentally minded. Young Southern U.S. woman (late teens–20s) with an associate’s degree, living with a partner in a small household, working full-time on a low income; politically moderate/independent and lightly religious. She is outgoing and socially confident but emotionally reactive and anxiety-prone, with a strong drive to keep relationships positive—highly empathetic, fairness-focused, and generally generous and trusting in social exchanges. Curious and open to new ideas with strong on-the-spot problem-solving, but less anchored in accumulated factual knowledge; she’s moderately analytical and financially literate, uses clear mental “budgets,” and tends toward risk-averse choices. She’s motivated by improvement and responsibility—especially being a strong role model for her child—while recognizing personal growth needs around organization, time management, calmness, and emotional control.

Married Black Catholic woman in the Midwest (30–49), high-school educated, working full-time on a low income in a 3-person household; politically independent but conservative and highly involved in church. She is emotionally intense and easily stressed, with very high anxiety/depressive tendencies, strong sensitivity to threat, and a strong desire for certainty and clear answers; she can be critical and blunt, not naturally cooperative, and tends to trust others very little. Financially she is highly risk-averse and very fairness/need focused: generous when terms feel fair but unwilling to give without control or obligation; she mentally budgets strictly, is impatient for near-term benefits, and is strongly shaped by immediate necessities rather than long-run ideals (including low interest in environmental causes).

Divorced white woman in her 50s–60s in the US West with an associate’s degree, unemployed, moderate income, atheist, and very liberal/Democrat. Socially outgoing, warm, and fairness-oriented; tends to share and cooperate, values equality, and is generally trusting while expecting equitable treatment. Curious and enjoys thinking through issues, but prefers clear answers and closure, often “maximizes” and second-guesses decisions; highly self-aware of how she comes across and adapts her behavior to social context. Low day-to-day structure and follow-through (struggles with motivation/consistency), and currently experiences high anxiety and depressive symptoms, with low confidence/clarity about who she is and how well she’s doing—leading to avoidance and worry about judgment. Financially and numerically average, somewhat impatient about delayed rewards, not minimalist (comfortable with more possessions/variety), moderately eco-leaning, and empathetic with a strong desire to leave things better than she found them.

Widowed Hispanic man in his 30s–40s living in the US South; self-employed, high-income, high-school educated, weekly religious attendee, and politically conservative/Republican. He’s highly risk-averse and prefers safe, predictable options, yet can be impatient about delayed rewards. Work style is inconsistent: he aspires to be organized and reliable, but in practice procrastinates, gets distracted, and follows through unevenly; he may benefit from structure and simple, actionable plans. Thinking style is more practical than intellectual—he doesn’t enjoy complex deliberation, relies on intuition, and overestimates his performance; he’s financially knowledgeable despite gaps in general knowledge/education. Emotionally he carries elevated anxiety and some depressive tone, with moderate self-certainty and low self-monitoring (less likely to adapt his presentation to others). Values lean agentic (self-advancement/independence) over communal bonding, with average interest in minimalism and a middling, not strongly ideological, pro-environment stance.

Midwestern white male (30–49), divorced, agnostic, politically moderate/independent, highly educated and high-earning, working full-time in a household of four. Cognitively, he enjoys thinking through complex problems and shows strong reflective reasoning, numeracy, and financial literacy; he uses clear mental “budgets” and categories for money, is moderately risk-averse, and somewhat impatient about delayed rewards. Socially and economically he prioritizes fairness and reciprocity (often offering generous splits and returning fair amounts), though he may still manage impressions and present himself in a socially acceptable way. Values emphasize independence, hard work, trustworthiness, courage, and continual learning; he’s self-aware about needing more compassion and patience and actively tries to improve.

Married Black man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western US, highly educated and high-income, working full-time and supporting a large household; Protestant who attends church occasionally and frames identity around being a faithful, loving, and financially responsible family leader. Socially confident, outgoing, cooperative, and highly disciplined/organized, with very low anxiety/depressive tendency and a clear, stable sense of self. Practical and tradition-leaning rather than novelty-seeking, prefers simplicity/minimalism, and likes clear answers and closure; adapts his presentation to context and is attentive to social norms (may answer in a socially desirable way). Strong quantitative/financial reasoning and reflective thinking; tends to be fair and reciprocity-minded—generous when giving and trusting, but unwilling to accept deals he deems unfair. Moderately pro-environment and politically moderate Democrat. Financial behavior can skew toward impulsive spending and impatience for delayed rewards, with otherwise average risk tolerance and relatively low sensitivity to losses.

Married Southern white woman (30–49), high-income and postgraduate educated, working full-time as a driven, detail-oriented CRNA; very conservative Republican and deeply involved in Protestant church life. Socially confident and assertive but not especially warm or naturally empathic; loyal to her in-group, values fairness and reciprocity, and is comfortable taking a leadership/mentor role. Highly conscientious, perfectionistic, and self-critical with some anxiety; strongly motivated by achievement and doing things “the right way,” prefers clear rules and certainty, and tends to over-optimize decisions rather than settle. Image- and context-aware (good self-monitoring) yet internally uncertain about identity, with a strong desire to stand out and a preference for minimalism. Numerically strong and practical, but less inclined toward abstract deliberation and can be overconfident in her judgments; money behavior skews tight/reluctant to spend despite comfort with strategic generosity and trust when reciprocity is expected. Environmentally minded and community-oriented, balancing ambition with duty, faith-based values, and a desire to make a meaningful positive impact.

Unemployed Hispanic woman in her 30s–40s in the Northeast, low income, high‑school educated, very liberal Democrat and nonreligious, living in a two‑person household. Quiet and socially withdrawn, not naturally cooperative or trusting at first, and low in drive for status or self-advancement; prefers autonomy and equality over group loyalty or hierarchy. Married Hispanic man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western U.S., high‑school educated, part‑time employed with a solid middle income; culturally Catholic but rarely attends, and strongly liberal/Democrat. He is notably risk-seeking and promotion-focused (drawn to upside and achievement), generally emotionally steady with low depression and average anxiety.

Midwest-based woman in her 50s–early 60s, college educated, Protestant and weekly churchgoer, politically independent but conservative, living in a two-person household with low income and currently unemployed. Highly outgoing, curious, and intellectually engaged—enjoys complex thinking, learning, and exploring options, and tends to “maximize” decisions rather than settle quickly; comfortable with ambiguity and may keep researching, which can create occasional indecision or feeling overwhelmed. Generally disciplined and reliability-oriented, with clear values and a desire to lead by example, though she can get distracted by too many competing tasks. Environmentally minded and numerate/analytical, but can be somewhat overconfident in her judgments and somewhat image-conscious in presenting herself positively. Financially, she’s more of a tightwad who dislikes spending, uses mental “budgets,” and is moderately patient about long-term tradeoffs; emotionally fairly steady with low anxiety/depressive tendencies.

Young Hispanic Catholic woman in the U.S. South (18–29), moderate Democrat, part-time worker with an associate’s degree, living in a 4-person household and is a mother; values family/community and shows strong empathy, fairness, and generosity, tending to share evenly and to trust others while also being somewhat cautious about being treated unfairly. Quiet and socially awkward/introverted but highly curious, creative, and open to new ideas; prefers collaboration and harmony over standing out, with low need to be unique and a generally grounded, honest response style. Decision-making: enjoys thinking and exploring possibilities and is comfortable with ambiguity, but often relies on intuition and may struggle with complex logic, numbers, and especially financial concepts; benefits from clear, simple, step-by-step guidance and practical examples for money decisions. Spending is slightly tightwad-leaning and uses mental “budgets” to organize gains/losses; aspires to be more confident, well-spoken, successful, and—given parenting responsibilities—more patient, responsible, and selfless.

Married Hispanic Catholic woman (30–49) in the Western US with postgraduate education, a homemaker in a four-person household and moderate/independent politics. She is organized, tidy, and responsibility-driven, prioritizing family stability and fairness, and tends to be nurturing and patient with her children while more easily irritated with her spouse; she aspires to stay calm, logical, manage time better, and build financial independence. Socially she is middle-of-the-road (not strongly outgoing), somewhat pragmatic rather than novelty-seeking, and values both getting ahead and maintaining harmony, with strong loyalty to her in-group and respect for family roles. Decision-wise she thinks things through and likes optimizing choices, but can be overconfident in her judgments and may present herself in a socially acceptable light; she prefers clear, structured options and is risk-averse, cautious with spending, and motivated by practical benefits more than environmental or minimalist ideals.

Male in his 50s–60s, Asian, West US, self-employed with low income, never married, agnostic/nonreligious, very conservative Republican. Highly disciplined, organized, and detail-focused; prefers structure, clear rules, and decisive conclusions, and tends to optimize rather than “good enough.” Quiet and socially reserved, low on warmth/compassion, skeptical of others’ motives, and strongly self-reliant—expects people to act in self-interest and is unlikely to extend trust or generosity without proof. Pragmatic minimalist and tightwad who avoids waste, is highly risk-averse, and prefers predictable outcomes; financially and numerically savvy and capable of reflective, logical thinking, leaning on accumulated knowledge and experience. Emotionally steady with low anxiety/depressive tendencies, strong self-concept, low desire to fit in or stand out, and little interest in environmental or “virtue-signaling” causes; communicates bluntly and is comfortable being disliked while focusing on minding his own business.

Self-employed, high-income Asian American man in his 50s–60s living in the US South; postgraduate educated, divorced, nonreligious, politically moderate/independent, in a two-person household. He is calm, emotionally steady, and low in anxiety/depressive tendencies, with a kind, cooperative, fairness-oriented style that shows up in generous sharing and high interpersonal trust/reciprocity. Socially he’s more reserved than outgoing, not very concerned with standing out, and not highly image-managing; he tends to be genuine and consistent with a clear sense of self. Cognitively he’s very knowledgeable and verbally/logically strong, enjoys thinking through complex issues, and is comfortable with ambiguity (low need for closure), often satisficing rather than obsessively optimizing. Young Asian American woman in the Western US (late teens/20s), college-educated, liberal/Democrat, atheist, currently unemployed and living in a large household. Divorced, middle-aged white woman in the Northeast with postgraduate education but currently unemployed and on a low income, living alone; politically independent but conservative and nonreligious. Young Asian American man in the Southern US, part-time employed with some college, moderate Democrat, loosely practicing Buddhist, living alone. Strongly self-advancing and status/achievement oriented, with a very high desire to stand out and a chameleon-like ability to manage impressions; motivated by self-improvement (especially fitness/attractiveness) but prone to procrastination and lower follow-through. Midwestern married white man (30–49) with an associate’s degree, high income, Protestant (attends monthly), politically independent but conservative. Black male in his 50s living in the US South, self-employed with some college, moderate income, never married, liberal/Democrat and nonreligious. Single, college-educated Jewish woman in her 50s living in the Western US, working full-time on a moderate income; politically conservative/Republican and not very environmentally oriented. Young Black woman in the South, high-income household, student, moderate Democrat with low religious identification but weekly attendance; socially outgoing in comfortable settings yet shy about public speaking and wants to become more outspoken, optimistic, and high-achieving (straight-A, big-organization career, eventual business). White married man in the Northeast, mid-career with a high-school education and solid middle income; liberal Democrat and atheist who rarely attends religious services. Midwestern Asian-American married man in his 30s–40s with a college/postgrad background, high income, and moderate Democratic politics; socially confident and assertive, emotionally steady, and generally reliable/discipline-oriented, with a strong drive for achievement and efficiency. Pragmatic and routine-leaning rather than novelty-seeking, he prefers clear, workable solutions over exploring many options, and tends to satisfice. Middle-aged Black man in the U.S. South, living alone and working full-time on a modest income; socially reserved and low on novelty-seeking, preferring familiar routines and practical, no-frills choices.
